A1.justification: Both PDFs describe causal differential networks (CDN), with matching methods and Appendices A-E. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and accompanying discussion.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on seven transcriptomics datasets and synthetic causal systems, including baseline comparisons, ablations, and uncertainty estimates.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds evaluations of perturbation-test-set variability and larger synthetic graphs.

M1.justification: The causal structure learner, differential network, input representations, graph and target losses, and training sequence are retained. The added FCI sampling specifications document the existing method rather than establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The seven biological datasets and synthetic mechanism/intervention families remain unchanged. v3 extends synthetic evaluation from 10- and 20-node systems to 100-node, 200-edge graphs in Table 11, adding a larger-input test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding biological and synthetic comparisons. Newly discussed related methods are not added as evaluated baselines; the new large-graph table reports CDN alone.

E3.justification: v3 adds five uniform K562 perturbation partitions, reported as 353 perturbations each versus the original 678-example test set, and a 100-node evaluation. Appendix D.1 also newly describes selecting genes by differential-expression p-value, conflicting with the log-fold-change criterion retained in Section 4.1. This documentation inconsistency does not establish an actual preprocessing change.

E4.justification: New Table 8 tests sensitivity to which K562 perturbations constitute the test set, while Table 11 tests performance on larger graphs. Existing graph-supervision, pretraining, node-statistics, and finetuning ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v3 adds uncertainty across five perturbation partitions and reports ten independent graphs for the new large-graph experiment. The earlier five-seed cell-subsampling analysis and five-graph synthetic uncertainty reporting remain unchanged; the ten-graph count concerns a new experiment.

E6.justification: Existing result entries are retained. New Table 8 reports normalized rank 0.974 on the original test set and 0.973 ± 0.009 across new partitions; Table 11 reports polynomial AUCs of 0.49-0.53 on larger graphs. Table 3 also adds two unexplained 'exclude scale' rows whose AUCs match large-graph linear/sigmoid results under incompatible 20-node/polynomial headings, leaving those rows' conditions unclear.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, and Appendix C constructions for hard and soft interventions are retained. Added explanations of existing metrics and biological limitations do not revise the formal analysis.

C1.justification: The central claims about supervised causal representations, perturbation-target prediction, and generalization across cell lines remain unchanged. The new Discussion restates the experimental-design motivation and existing technical contribution.

C2.justification: Beyond the retained chemical-perturbation caveats, new Section 5 substantially expands applicability boundaries: cyclic feedback, temporal dynamics, unobserved confounding, and synthetic-to-real distribution shift. Appendix E additionally interprets large-graph failures through possible graph-prediction error propagation and explains stronger linear-soft performance through summary statistics.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link and specifies FCI subset size k = 5, estimate count T = 100, and correlation-based subset sampling. These improve implementation disclosure without demonstrating changed training settings.

R1.justification: Sections 2.2-2.3 expand coverage of historical expression-based approaches, foundation models, and causal-change detection. v3 explicitly relates CDN to earlier data-driven target inference by di Bernardo et al. and Noh and Gunawan, distinguishing its nonlinear relationships. Publication updates to retained works are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: v3 adds a Discussion section, expands selected background and method explanations, clarifies metric descriptions, and introduces descriptive subheadings in Appendix D.1. Most existing prose and the main section/appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 8 and 11 and two rows to Table 3, while relocating retained displays. It fixes overlapping captions and headers in Tables 4-6. All eleven figures retain their underlying visual content.

improvement.justification: The added implementation details, robustness/scaling evidence, explicit biological limitations, and repaired table captions modestly improve reproducibility and assessment of applicability. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems, but the conflicting gene-selection descriptions and unexplained Table 3 rows limit the improvement. The core method and retained results remain unchanged.
